solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Term for driver in police tactical unit

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the word for the police that follows

parts.note: cops are police officers

indicators.note: a term is an end, so this asks for the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the end letter of driver

explanation.surface: A question about what officers in a police tactical squad call their driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The end letter of 'driver' goes inside COPS to give CORPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A corps is an army formation, a military unit organised for a particular tactical role.

clue.text: Possibly saloon lawsuit remains

parts.note: a saloon is one kind of car
a case is a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.surface: A lawsuit about a saloon bar, or a car, seems to leave something behind.
explanation.walkthrough: CARCASE is an older spelling of carcass. A saloon is a car with a fixed roof, what Americans call a sedan.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcase is a dead body, the bodily remains of an animal.

clue.text: Take out cracking bit of lamb with a bone

indicators.note: something cracking is breaking up, so the word before it is broken and reset

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for 'take', on prescriptions
the letters of out, cracked open

indicators.note: a bit of a word here is just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of lamb
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook removes a bone that has split a piece of lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' reads like one verb; it splits into R (the prescription 'take') and an anagram of OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotula is the kneecap, the patella, a small bone at the front of the knee.

clue.text: Utter excitedly about joining Royal Engineers

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for excited is read from its end

parts.note: to be up is to be excited, as in worked up
RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Someone talks excitedly about signing up with the army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb of speaking; it is the adjective meaning complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure and utter are both intensifying adjectives meaning absolute, as in pure nonsense or utter nonsense.

clue.text: A stiff-upper-lip sort giving endless criticism about nowt

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shortened word wraps the nothing
without an end, so the word for criticism loses its last letter

parts.note: to give someone stick is to criticise them
nowt is northern English for nothing, which is O

explanation.surface: A stiff-upper-lip type delivers nonstop criticism over nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: STICK loses its K and wraps O.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic endures hardship without complaint, which is exactly what keeping a stiff upper lip describes.

clue.text: Yank holding power secure in the Act of Union?

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so the word for yank grips the rest

parts.note: to yank is to tug
P is the symbol for power
to pin is to fasten securely

explanation.surface: An American seizes control to guarantee the Act of Union that joined Britain's nations.
explanation.walkthrough: The Acts of Union joined England and Scotland; the question mark warns that this union is a ram mating with a ewe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tupping is a ram mating with a ewe, a jocular reading of an act of union.

clue.text: Unlikely tale lifting the lid on headdress — wow! This is pulled off

indicators.note: removing the lid takes off the top, the first letter of the headdress word

parts.note: a turban is a wrapped headdress

indicators.note: pulled off means removed, so those two letters come out of the word this

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise
taken as written

explanation.surface: A far-fetched story about someone whose turban gets knocked off.
explanation.walkthrough: TURBAN loses its T, then THIS loses IS.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban myth is a widely repeated modern story that is untrue, an unlikely tale.

clue.text: Malevolent Persian being against dance

parts.note: a peri in Persian myth was at first an evil spirit, later a fairy
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A spiteful Persian objects to dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Persian being' reads as one phrase but 'being' just joins PERI to CON.
explanation.definitionFit: The pericon is a folk dance of Argentina and Uruguay, performed by couples.

clue.text: At home with good butter? Thick, as it was

parts.note: in means at home
G is short for good
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: Someone at home asks whether good butter used to be thick.
explanation.walkthrough: A butter here is one who butts, not the dairy spread. 'As it was' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingram is an old word for ignorant, and thick is slang for stupid or ignorant.

clue.text: Fancy the new air? It's virtually colourless

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Do you like the fresh air? It's almost clear of any tint.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-white is almost white, a pale shade with barely any colour in it.

clue.text: German on preposterous way of cheek

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German

indicators.note: preposterous literally means having the before after, back to front

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: A German behaves absurdly with a cheeky manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preposterous' is used in its Latin sense, before-after, so the word for way is turned back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Genal is the anatomical adjective relating to the cheek, from Latin gena.

clue.text: ____ played away from home, European taken in by randy raver

indicators.note: being taken in means being placed inside another word
randy means wild with lust, so the word after it is in disorder

parts.note: the letters to rearrange around the rest
out means away from home
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A clue with a blank: someone was unfaithful, a European seduced by a lusty partygoer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the blank as 'one who': one who played away, that is, cheated on a spouse. 'From home' does double duty in the surface but here means out.
explanation.definitionFit: Avouterer is an archaic word for adulterer, and playing away is slang for being sexually unfaithful.

clue.text: Who arranges westbound rockets

indicators.note: in an across entry going west means running right to left

parts.note: one who arranges things in order sorts them

explanation.surface: A question about who organises rockets heading west.
explanation.definitionFit: Retros are retro-rockets, small rockets fired against a craft's motion to slow it.

clue.text: Scots jag an item of footwear

parts.note: brog is Scots for a prod or jab, which is what a jag is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot gives a jab to a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jag' looks like slang for a Jaguar car or a drinking spree; here it is a prick or jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogan is a heavy, coarse leather shoe or ankle boot.

clue.text: Height of delight about English verse

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for delight wraps the other two letters

parts.note: elation is great delight
E is the abbreviation for English
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: The peak of pleasure found in English poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Height of delight' reads as one phrase, but 'of' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation is a height above a level, such as of ground above the sea.

clue.text: A long-standing producer of oil will video flaring

indicators.note: flaring means bursting into wild flames, so the letters scatter and regroup

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone will film a veteran oil well as it bursts into flame.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an oil well; the producer is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild olive is a tree, long-lived and yielding olives from which oil is pressed.

clue.text: Insides of transistor radios left over in Lossiemouth

indicators.note: the insides of a phrase are letters sitting within it, across the word break

parts.note: the letters straddle the gap between the two words, the tail of one and the head of the next

explanation.surface: The innards of old transistor radios lie about unused in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Lossiemouth is a town in north-east Scotland, so the definition asks for a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Orra is Scots for odd or spare, meaning surplus and left over.

clue.text: Cold, then one'll stuff comprehensive antibiotic

indicators.note: to stuff something is to fill its inside, so these letters go into the next word

parts.note: all-in means comprehensive, including everything
C is the abbreviation for cold
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: You've got a cold, so a broad-spectrum antibiotic will be stuffed into you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One'll' is read as 'one will', and 'will stuff' signals putting C and I inside ALL IN, a word for comprehensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Allicin is the compound in crushed garlic with antibacterial action, hence an antibiotic.

clue.text: Such as keeps lobster fresh in Sri Lanka

definitions.text: Such as keeps lobster fresh in Sri Lanka

parts.note: surface reading: some kind of chilling or storage method for seafood
setter's reading: a pen in water where live shellfish are held, and also the enclosure, a kraal, used to trap elephants in Sri Lanka

explanation.walkthrough: The word is the old Dutch-derived noun for an enclosure, not the verb of slow movement or the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawl is an enclosure in shallow water for keeping fish, turtles or lobsters alive, related to kraal.

clue.text: Certain swimmer inaptly, we hear, grasps nut for the biggest part

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, so its final letter goes
what we hear is a word's sound, so the spelling may differ

parts.note: to grasp is to seize
an almond is a nut

explanation.surface: Some fish is clumsily said to grab a nut for most of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inaptly' belongs to the definition: the fish called sea salmon is not a true salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea salmon is a name given to several fish, such as the Australian salmon, that are not true salmon.

clue.text: Charles de Gaulle, eg, left pressed by publicity

parts.note: to give something air is to publicise it
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: General de Gaulle was abandoned, squeezed by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'pressed by' puts the word for publicity on top of the other. Charles de Gaulle is the main airport of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle is the name of the major airport serving Paris, an example of the category.

clue.text: Balmoral or other stuck into mature woman's guru

indicators.note: stuck into means pushed inside, so the hat sits in the middle

parts.note: mama is a mother, a mature woman
a balmoral is a Scottish bonnet, one hat among others

explanation.surface: A royal Scottish castle or another lodged in an elderly woman's spiritual teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral sounds like the royal castle in Scotland; here it is the flat Scottish bonnet named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, meaning great soul, is an honorific for a revered spiritual teacher, like a guru.

clue.text: Young thug is to stand up and will make a break for it

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read from bottom to top

indicators.text: will make a break for it
indicators.note: making a break for it means escaping, so the word and leaves

parts.note: the words taken as written; the letters left once one word escapes run backwards in the clue only by coincidence, so this is not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A young hoodlum is told to get to his feet and duly tries to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters AND escape from IS TO STAND, leaving ISTOST, which then reads upwards. A tsotsi is a South African township gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsotsi is South African slang for a young urban criminal or gang member, a thug.

clue.text: Class of plant: first-rate, umpteen carried out from the east

indicators.note: reading from the east in an across entry means from right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with 1 read as I
umpteen means a great many
to carry out a task is to do it

explanation.surface: A type of plant, first-class, is shipped out in huge numbers from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: AI, MANY and DID are joined and then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Didynamia was a Linnaean class of plants with four stamens in two unequal pairs.

clue.text: Cartoon girlfriend that delivers eggs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the mouse who is Mickey's girlfriend in Disney cartoons
second meaning: soldiers' slang for a German trench mortar, whose bombs were called eggs

explanation.walkthrough: Eggs suggests a hen; it is slang for bombs, and the trench mortar is the Minenwerfer, shortened by British troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnie Mouse is Mickey's cartoon sweetheart, and a minnie was a First World War German mortar firing bombs.

clue.text: This stunner taken aback posed again

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to sit again for a portrait is to resit, past tense resat

explanation.surface: A stunning model was surprised when asked to pose a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a beautiful model; it is a device that stuns.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric stun gun, a weapon that stuns, so a stunner.

clue.text: Get money from a small snack

parts.note: to tap someone is to ask them for money
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Borrowing cash off someone for a little bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish savoury dishes, eaten as a snack with drinks.

clue.text: What's in motor? Scotsman's joint! It helps to stay steady

indicators.note: what is in a word is its interior, everything but the outer letters

parts.note: the inner letters of motor
lith is Scots for a joint or segment

explanation.surface: A car's engine, a Scotsman's spliff: something to keep you calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a cannabis cigarette; it is a body joint, in Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: An otolith is a tiny chalky particle in the inner ear that senses gravity and helps balance.

clue.text: Open University being for chaps from Jo'burg

parts.note: OU is the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university
ens is a philosophical term for being or entity

explanation.surface: The Open University exists for South African men.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouens is the plural of ou, South African slang for a man or bloke, used in Johannesburg.

clue.text: A tiny bit a hustler

parts.note: taken as written
tom is slang for a prostitute, a hustler

explanation.surface: Someone is only a little bit of a con artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hustler' suggests a swindler; it is a prostitute, slang tom.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest particle, so figuratively a minute amount.

clue.text: Dear mortal

definitions.meaning: second meaning: very drunk, as mortal is used in slang

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a letter's salutation to a human; both words are adjectives with slang senses.
explanation.definitionFit: High prices are costly ones, and high and mortal both describe someone heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Weight of one's jugs

parts.note: pith means substance or weight, as of an argument
o' is a shortened of, as in o'clock
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: How heavy are a person's jugs?
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of one's only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithoi are large earthenware storage jars of ancient Greece, the plural of pithos.

clue.text: Muck in bin, tie tightly

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Put the filth in the dustbin and tie it up securely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muck' looks like dirt going in the bin; 'muck in' is a phrasal verb meaning join in.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in it is to take part, which is what mucking in means: sharing in the work.

clue.text: Blessed Virgin is foremost in maternal doctrine

indicators.note: blessed is a mild curse, so the words are knocked about

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the foremost letter is the very first one of a word

parts.note: first letter of maternal

explanation.surface: The Blessed Virgin is central to the teaching of motherhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blessed Virgin' reads as Mary; 'blessed' is a mild curse word.
explanation.definitionFit: Irvingism is the doctrine of Edward Irving's Catholic Apostolic Church, a religious teaching.

clue.text: Spoil mitts being back in strong breeze

indicators.note: back means returning, so the string is read from right to left

parts.note: to ret is to rot or spoil, as with flax soaked too long
fins and mitts are both slang for hands

explanation.surface: A gale ruins your gloves being returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mitts' suggests gloves; here both it and fins are slang for hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A snifter is a strong breeze in Scots and dialect use, as well as a small drink.

clue.text: Month for Jews taking time off in old Yemen

indicators.note: taking off means removing, so the letter for time leaves the month

parts.note: Shebat is a month in the Jewish calendar

explanation.surface: Jews take a month of holiday in ancient Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was the ancient kingdom in south Arabia, roughly modern Yemen, ruled by the Queen of Sheba.
